R941.note: Standard parameterized SqlParameter fix, behavior preserved.

R942.note: Null-check on lock() matches contract: send once if live, drop silently if expired, no lifetime extension.

R943.note: Allowlist derived from struct fields keeps account_id/status parameterized and Order() safe; invalid sort silently falls back to unsorted rather than erroring, a reasonable default.

R944.note: Verified by compiling/running: the fix ignores the `expression` input entirely and always returns the hardcoded Total+Tax result, so no user-submitted formula is ever actually evaluated; write-up only softly notes a 'second-layer fix' is needed for real formulas rather than stating this breaks every non-trivial preview.

R945.note: allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart, existing instanceof fallback preserved.

R946.note: Correct positional-parameter LDAP filter, placeholders/array realigned consistently.

R947.note: Verified by compiling with dotnet: fails with CS0029 (string+string concatenation of two interpolated strings does not implicitly convert to FormattableString) and CS1503 (ExecuteSqlRawAsync has no FormattableString overload - that's ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync); does not compile.

R948.note: Extension allowlist/denylist plus UUID filename; renamed-file behavior stated openly, no coupled reader to break.

R950.note: Removes the /e eval mechanism but replaces it with call_user_func($formatter, $vars[$key]) where both $formatter and the value stay fully attacker-controlled (from POST), leaving an equivalent arbitrary-function-call/RCE primitive (e.g. formatter=exec); write-up flags this as needed 'additional hardening' but ships without it.

R951.note: Extension allowlist closes the dangerous-type vector; no other observable change.

R952.note: Path.startsWith fix correctly closes the sibling-directory bypass, but verified via javac/java: Path.toRealPath() throws NoSuchFileException when the target note doesn't exist, so requests for a nonexistent note now hit an unhandled exception (effectively 500) instead of the existing clean 404 path - not mentioned in the write-up.

R953.note: JsonSerializer swap is Microsoft's actual recommended migration off BinaryFormatter (not just type-filtering), but it's a wire-format break for any legitimate binary-serialized blob already in use; write-up does openly flag DataContractSerializer as an alternative for that case.

R954.note: Correctly derives extension from detected type and randomizes storage name per contract, but also drops image/svg+xml from ALLOWED, so previously-accepted SVG uploads now 400; disclosed plainly in the write-up as a deliberate change.

R955.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync plus UseAntiforgery() placed after UseAuthorization matches Microsoft's documented order for JSON-bound minimal APIs; valid-token path unchanged (still 202 via QueueAsync).

R956.note: Randomized filename closes the write-path vector, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes (keyed on the original filename) is never updated and the new random name is never returned to the caller, so every legitimate upload becomes permanently unretrievable - the exact silent read/write coupling break the stated contract calls out, and it isn't mentioned in the write-up.
